'''Suzanne Soraya Fernandes-Sindi''' is an American applied mathematician whose research uses mathematics and [[machine learning]] to model biological phenomena including [[prion]] aggregation, [[coagulation|blood coagulation]], [[population dynamics]], and [[structural variation]].{{r|smb}} She is a professor of applied mathematics in the School of Natural Sciences at the [[University of California, Merced]],{{r|dir}} and the former chair of the Department of Applied Mathematics at UC Merced.{{r|bio}} She chairs the Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion Activity Group of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]].{{r|siag}}

==Early life and education==
Sindi is originally from [[Placentia, California]]; her parents were immigrants from Saudi Arabia and from the [[Azores]] of Portugal.{{r|bio}} She describes her interest in mathematical biology as inspired by reading the 1990 novel ''[[Jurassic Park (novel)|Jurassic Park]]'' as a middle school student.{{r|smb}} As an undergraduate at [[California State University, Fullerton]], she received a National Science Foundation Graduate Fellowship,{{r|nsf}} funding her graduate study at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]]. There, she received a master's degree in 2004 and completed her Ph.D. in 2006.{{r|dir}} Her doctoral dissertation, ''Describing and Modeling Repetitive Sequences in DNA'', was supervised by [[James A. Yorke]].{{r|mg}}

==Recognition==
Sindi was named as a Fellow of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]], in the 2027 class of fellows, "for her sustained national leadership in advancing women and underrepresented groups in the mathematical sciences through founding Cal-Bridge Mathematics, her stewardship of the Workshops for Women in Mathematical Biology, and her inclusive departmental leadership as Chair of UC Merced Applied Mathematics".{{r|fawm}}
